summary: Toshiya Unebe works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Musashi Tachikawa and served as Associate Professor in the Department of Indian Studies at Nagoya University's Graduate School of Letters (attested 2006–2011).

Totsudo Kato worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Oriental Hall, Kyoto Horitsu Gakko, and Chuo University under Seiran Ouchi, Enryo Inoue, and Bankon Shimada, later teaching at Shakutoku Kyoko, Setagaya Gakuen, Komazawa, Toyo, and Nihon universities.

Touhoi Fok was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied at the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies, Otani University, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong, where he served as a lecturer from circa 1972 to 1999.

Touraj Daryaee specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of California, Los Angeles from circa 1993 to 1999 and held a post at the University of California, Irvine around 2007.

Towao Sakaehara is a historian and Japanologist who earned his degrees, including a doctorate, at Kyoto University between 1965 and 1993. He held posts at Otemon Gakuin University, Osaka City University (1981–2010), and the Osaka Museum of History (2014–2020).

Travis L. Smith specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at UC Berkeley and Columbia University (PhD 2007) under several scholars, later holding posts at Barnard College, the University of Florida (attested 2012), and UC Berkeley (attested 2026).
Trent Walker works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, where he studied under Alexander von Rospatt.

Trevor Leggett worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Indology. He studied at King's College London, the University of London, and SOAS under Hari Prasad Shastri, Arthur Waley, and Yukio Tani, later heading the BBC Japanese Service (circa 1946–1970).

Trijang Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Gyuto Monastery and under masters including Phabongkha Dechen Nyingpo. He succeeded Ling Rinpoche and taught many prominent disciples, including the 14th Dalai Lama.

Trine Brox specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA under the supervision of Christian K. Wedemeyer and holds an Associate Professor post at the University of Copenhagen (attested 2026).
Trinle Lhundrub studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.
Tro Shul Khenpo Jampal Dorjé studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Troy Organ was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Iowa (circa 1937–1941). He held academic posts at Chatham University, Parsons College, the University of Akron, and Ohio University.

Trulshik Rinpoche was a Buddhist and Tibetan studies figure who studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, and others. He taught numerous students, including the 14th Dalai Lama, Adam Pearcey, and Phakchok Rinpoche.

Trulshik Rinpoche Ngawang Chökyi Lodrö was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He taught the 14th Dalai Lama and Sogyal Rinpoche, founded Thubten Chöling, and became the official head of Nyingma in 2010.
Trung Huynh is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the University of the West under the doctoral supervision of Darui Long (attested 2016).

Trungram Gyaltrul Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute and Harvard University (PhD circa 1997–2004) under Leonard van der Kuijp, founding the United Trungram Buddhist Foundation and Fellowship.

Trungram Gyalwa Rinpoche specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Harvard University (PhD 2004), later serving as a visiting scholar at Michigan and visiting professor at McGill (2016).

Tryambak Shankar Shejwalkar was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Mumbai from circa 1913 to 1917. He served on the faculty at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute from circa 1939 to 1955.

Tryambakarama Sastri specialized in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University under Lakshmana Sastri Dravida and served as head of Government Sanskrit Pathashala in Jamnagar (attested 1932).
